embodiment_body_ownership.evidence: The scarf hand at image left connects through its white cuff and robe sleeve to the woman; the wand hand at image right connects to her opposite wrist and sleeve. No consequential detached limb is visible.

embodiment_joint_chain_and_reach.evidence: Both forearms rise to reachable collarbone/shoulder positions. Bent fingers wrap the scarf and wand with connected wrist chains and coherent finger curvature.

embodiment_support_and_balance.evidence: Her visible torso is upright without a conflicting support claim, and the complete hat rests on the flat stone pedestal top. Floor support is below the portrait crop and remains physically compatible.

embodiment_contact_and_space.evidence: Right fingers contact knitted scarf fabric, left fingers wrap the wooden wand grip, and neither hand penetrates the hat or pedestal. Clear elbow/prop space separates the actions.

embodiment_visibility_and_projection.evidence: Face, both important hands, wand tip and the entire hat support area remain assessable in the saved frame. The critical grip relations are legible despite ordinary finger overlap.

user_judgment.evidence: No direct requesting-user acceptance has been received.

supplemental_observations.blind_impression: A warm cinematic wizarding-school ceremony portrait, dominated by the familiar face, textured red-gold knitwear and a tactile grumpy-faced textile hat.
weaknesses: The star field occupies high wall/window-like arch panels rather than an unambiguously continuous overhead ceiling.
The hand is lit diffusely; source-specific light spill from the wand tip onto the upper fingers is not separable from ambient light.
supplemental_observations.control_comparison: The quiet direct look and soft facial light read as subtle supporting attraction. Costume and magical environment remain the principal narrative; no added fetish expression is apparent.
